name: TX-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+23 partisan lean in the Texas Panhandle
Incumbent advantage with no polls or outside opposition
model.rationale: The district's R+23 lean, Ronny Jackson's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and Polymarket pricing the Democrat at 4% all point to a safe Republican hold; Nair's minimal fundraising offers no evidence of competitiveness.
model.watch: A late scandal or unexpected national wave could tighten the race, but nothing in the evidence suggests it will.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-13 is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Incumbent Ronny Jackson is running for reelection and holds a massive financial advantage, having raised over $4 million and holding $5.4 million on hand, with modest outside support and no outside opposition. Challenger Mark Nair has raised about $102,000 with only $14,000 remaining.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Jackson roughly a 95% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money, and district lean all align, making this a safe Republican seat with little evidence of a competitive contest.
